question.problem: Given that $X∼\text{Bernoulli}(0.1)$ and $Y∼\text{Bernoulli}(0.8)$ are independent, calculate $P(X=0\,\cup \,Y=0).$
question.worked_solution:
By the addition law, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X=0\,\cup \,Y=0) & =P(X=0)+P(Y=0)-P(X=0\,\cap \,Y=0).\end{aligned}
$$

Using the multiplication law for independent events, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X=0\,\cap \,Y=0) & =P(X=0)\cdot P(Y=0).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X=0\,\cup \,Y=0) & =P(X=0)+P(Y=0)-P(X=0)\cdot P(Y=0).\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $X∼\text{Bernoulli}(0.1),$ we have

$$
P(X=1)=0.1,\,P(X=0)=0.9,
$$

and since $Y∼\text{Bernoulli}(0.8),$ we have

$$
P(Y=1)=0.8,\,P(Y=0)=0.2.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X=0\,\cup \,Y=0) & =P(X=0)+P(Y=0)-P(X=0)\cdot P(Y=0) \\  & =0.9+0.2-0.9\cdot 0.2 \\  & =1.1-0.18 \\  & =0.92.\end{aligned}
$$
